To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the basic reproductive number of the age-structure HIV infection models without (or with drug treatment) is determined by the burst sizes, and the global asymptotic stabilities of the infection-free and infected steady states depend only on the basic reproduction number.
the basic reproductive number is a threshold quantity, and the infection-free equilibrium and the endemic equilibrium are globally asymptotically stable if and only if R0<1 and R0>1, respectively.
the basic reproductive number is the key factor determining the dynamical properties of age-structured models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new age-structured model for HIV infection and the dynamical properties of this model are established.
the global dynamics of the age-structure HIV infection models.
the global stability of the age- structured population model describing the basic HIV infection process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the basic reproductive number of the age-structure model is equivalent to that of the ODE or DDE model, and the global stability of the infection steady state of the age-structural model is equivalent to the global stability of that of the ODA (ordinary differential equation) and DDE model.
the age-structured PDE model can be used to describe the HIV infection process.
the age structure of the HIV infection model has no effect on its dynamical properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PDE model is a natural and general model of HIV infection, and the ODE and DDF models are two special cases of it.
the age-structured PDE model is more realistic and can provide more information than the ODE model and DDE model.
the age-structured population models can unify the typical ODEs and DDEs in the literature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the age-structured PDE model can be used as a unifying framework for the study of HIV infection models.
the PDE models are able to capture the dynamics of the infection process more accurately than the corresponding ODE and DED models.
